title_en: Enforcement Case of Compulsory Acquisition of Shares Held by Guangdong Hengtong Group Co., Ltd. to Offset Its Debt
keywords_en: Civil; Enforcement; Shareholder Tort; First Instance; Intermediate People's Court; Jiangsu Province; Shanghai; Guangdong Province; Legal Person; Company Law; Civil Procedure Law; Controlling shareholder's overvaluation of assets for debt repayment; Company's acquisition of its own shares; Compulsory enforcement of shares to repay debt; In favor of plaintiff; Controlling shareholder's infringement; Debt settlement with assets; Inability to auction or sell shares; Compulsory acquisition of shares; Principle of fairness; Good faith
full_text_en:
Enforcement Case of Compulsory Acquisition of Shares Held by Guangdong Hengtong Group Co., Ltd. to Offset Its Debts

Applicant for Enforcement: Wuxi Nanchang District Real Estate Management Company, Jiangsu Province. Domicile: Qingyang Road, Wuxi.
Legal Representative: Lu Suobao, Manager of the Company.

Applicant for Enforcement: Shanghai Pudong State-owned Assets Investment Management Co., Ltd. Domicile: South Pudong Road, Shanghai.
Legal Representative: Zhang Zhe, Chairman of the Board of the Company.

Applicant for Enforcement: Wuxi Xinjiangnan Industrial Co., Ltd., Jiangsu Province. Domicile: Tongyang Road, Wuxi.
Legal Representative: Zhang Shaojie, Chairman of the Board of the Company.

Enforcee: Guangdong Hengtong Group Co., Ltd. Domicile: Gongbei Zhongjian Building, Zhuhai City, Guangdong Province.
Legal Representative: Yang Bo, Chairman of the Board of the Company.

The plaintiffs, Wuxi Nanchang District Real Estate Management Company, Jiangsu Province (hereinafter referred to as Nanchang Company), Shanghai Pudong State-owned Assets Investment Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Pudong Company), and the defendant, Guangdong Hengtong Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hengtong Company), are all shareholders of the third party, Wuxi Xinjiangnan Industrial Co., Ltd., Jiangsu Province (hereinafter referred to as Xinjiangnan Company). Among the registered capital of RMB 80 million of Xinjiangnan Company, Hengtong Company holds RMB 44 million in shares, making it the controlling shareholder of Xinjiangnan Company; Nanchang Company holds RMB 14.5 million in shares, Pudong Company holds RMB 4 million in shares, and the remaining shares are held by various minority shareholders. Hengtong Company appointed Zhang Shaojie as Chairman of the Board and legal representative of Xinjiangnan Company, and upon Zhang Shaojie's nomination, appointed Shi Guixiang of Hengtong Company as General Manager of Xinjiangnan Company.

On August 20, 1998, the defendant Hengtong Company and the third party Xinjiangnan Company signed a "Debt and Creditor's Rights Settlement Agreement," confirming that as of June 30, 1998, Hengtong Company owed Xinjiangnan Company RMB 39.71 million. Hengtong Company used its properties, including Building No. 13, Dormitory Buildings No. 9, No. 10, and No. 12, totaling 17,897.04 square meters in the Shangshuijing Industrial Zone, Shenzhen, valued at RMB 40,352,784, to offset its debts to Xinjiangnan Company. The balance of RMB 642,784 after the offset was to be used as property transfer fees.

After the agreement was signed, because Building No. 13 was sealed up by the Hainan High People's Court, the defendant Hengtong Company transferred the other properties to the third party Xinjiangnan Company. On May 6, 1999, the second session of the fourth board meeting of Xinjiangnan Company resolved: to instruct the management team to organize an appraisal of the properties used by Hengtong Company to offset debts. If the appraised value depreciated, it would be offset by Hengtong Company's equity. Xinjiangnan Company commissioned Wuxi Hengmao Real Estate Appraisal Firm (hereinafter referred to as Hengmao Firm) to conduct the appraisal. The appraisal determined that the value of Hengtong Company's properties used to offset debts was RMB 25,168,800. Accordingly, the non-controlling shareholders of Xinjiangnan Company believed that Hengtong Company, by taking advantage of its dominant position as Chairman and General Manager of Xinjiangnan Company, had used properties appraised at only RMB 25,168,800 to offset debts valued at over RMB 40.35 million, thereby harming the interests of Xinjiangnan Company and themselves. They decided to sue Hengtong Company for infringement. However, since Hengtong Company was the controlling shareholder of Xinjiangnan Company, Xinjiangnan Company could not form a resolution at the board meeting to sue Hengtong Company. Therefore, the non-controlling shareholders entrusted Nanchang Company and Pudong Company as their representatives to file an infringement lawsuit against Hengtong Company. During the litigation, Hengtong Company raised objections to the appraisal report of Hengmao Firm, and the court commissioned Shenzhen Hongsha Real Estate Transaction Appraisal Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hongsha Company) to conduct a reappraisal. Hongsha Company appraised the properties based on the benchmark value as of August 20, 1998 (the date of the agreement between Hengtong Company and Xinjiangnan Company). After deducting the properties that had been sealed up by the Hainan High People's Court and executed to others, the remaining properties used by Hengtong Company to offset debts to Xinjiangnan Company were appraised at RMB 11,197,400. The appraisal fee of RMB 19,800 was advanced by Nanchang Company and Pudong Company.

After trial, the Wuxi Intermediate People's Court held that the actual value of the properties used by the defendant Hengtong Company to offset debts to the third party Xinjiangnan Company was only RMB 11,197,400, which was far insufficient to offset its debt of RMB 39.71 million to Xinjiangnan Company. Hengtong Company, utilizing its controlling position in Xinjiangnan Company and by means of offsetting debts with properties and overvaluing low-value assets, sought illegal benefits for itself, causing losses of RMB 28,512,600 to Xinjiangnan Company and infringing upon the rights and interests of Xinjiangnan Company and other non-controlling shareholders. The provisions of the Debt and Creditor's Rights Settlement Agreement signed by Hengtong Company and Xinjiangnan Company on August 20, 1998, concerning Hengtong Company's use of properties valued to offset debts to Xinjiangnan Company, violated the principles of fairness and good faith and should be deemed invalid. Hengtong Company shall be liable for compensating the losses caused to Xinjiangnan Company by its infringing acts. Accordingly, the court ruled:

1. The defendant Hengtong Company shall pay the third party Xinjiangnan Company RMB 28,512,600 plus interest (calculated from August 20, 1998, at the overdue loan interest rate of the same period) as of the date this judgment takes effect.

2. The defendant Hengtong Company shall pay the plaintiffs Nanchang Company and Pudong Company the property appraisal fee of RMB 19,800 advanced by them as of the date this judgment takes effect. The case acceptance fee of RMB 152,573 and the property preservation fee of RMB 125,000, totaling RMB 277,573, shall be borne by the defendant Hengtong Company.

Hengtong Company appealed against the first-instance judgment. Later, because the company failed to pay the second-instance case acceptance fee on time, the Jiangsu High People's Court ruled that the appeal shall be deemed automatically withdrawn, and the original judgment shall take effect.

After the first-instance judgment took effect, the defendant Hengtong Company did not voluntarily perform the payment obligations determined in the judgment. On November 10, 2000, the plaintiffs Nanchang Company and Pudong Company and the third party Xinjiangnan Company applied for enforcement to the Wuxi Intermediate People's Court.

Upon receiving the enforcement application, the Wuxi Intermediate People's Court accepted the case in accordance with the law and served an enforcement notice to the enforcee Hengtong Company. During enforcement, it was learned that apart from the shares it held in Xinjiangnan Company, Hengtong Company had no other property available for enforcement. Therefore, on January 16, 2001, the court sealed up 40 million shares of Xinjiangnan Company held by Hengtong Company and commissioned Wuxi Puxin Certified Public Accountants to appraise the value of these shares. The appraisal determined that the net asset value per share of Xinjiangnan Company was approximately RMB 0.92.

On April 16, 2001, the Wuxi Intermediate People's Court commissioned Wuxi East China Auction House Co., Ltd. to auction the sealed-up 40 million shares of Xinjiangnan Company. The auction was unsuccessful, and the shares could not be sold by other means.

At this point, the total principal and interest owed by the enforcee Hengtong Company to the applicant for enforcement Xinjiangnan Company, as well as the litigation costs, property preservation fees, enforcement fees, and appraisal fees advanced by Xinjiangnan Company and its non-controlling shareholders, had reached RMB 36,426,331.

After study, the Wuxi Intermediate People's Court held that the debt owed by the enforcee Hengtong Company was primarily to the applicant for enforcement Xinjiangnan Company. However, the only property recovered in enforcement was the 40 million shares of Xinjiangnan Company held by Hengtong Company, which could not be auctioned or sold. The only option was for Xinjiangnan Company to repurchase them to offset Hengtong Company's debts to it. Article 149 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "A company shall not purchase its own shares, except for the purpose of reducing its capital by cancelling shares or merging with another company holding its shares." "After purchasing its own shares in accordance with the provisions of the preceding paragraph, the company must cancel such shares within ten days, register the change in accordance with the law and administrative regulations, and make a public announcement." "A company shall not accept its own shares as collateral for a mortgage." From this provision, it can be seen that under normal circumstances, a company cannot purchase its own shares, but under special circumstances, the law allows a company to purchase its own shares in accordance with statutory procedures. If Xinjiangnan Company were to purchase the shares held by Hengtong Company, then Hengtong Company's shares in Xinjiangnan Company would be cancelled, and the capital of Xinjiangnan Company would necessarily be reduced, thereby meeting the special requirements of the law for purchasing the company's own shares. However, to achieve this step, it must be authorized by a resolution of the shareholders' meeting of Xinjiangnan Company. Hengtong Company remains the controlling shareholder of Xinjiangnan Company, and Xinjiangnan Company cannot pass such a resolution at the shareholders' meeting. In order to uphold the dignity of the law, regulate and improve the joint stock company system, protect the legitimate rights and interests of all shareholders of the joint stock company in accordance with the law, and sanction infringing acts occurring within the company, the only recourse is for the People's Court to compel Xinjiangnan Company to purchase the shares of Xinjiangnan Company held by Hengtong Company. Accordingly, pursuant to item (11) of Article 140, paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Wuxi Intermediate People's Court ruled on April 28, 2001:

The debt of RMB 36,426,331 owed by Xinjiangnan Company to Hengtong Company shall be used as the purchase price to compulsorily acquire the 39,593,838 shares of Xinjiangnan Company held by Hengtong Company. After the acquisition, Xinjiangnan Company shall correspondingly reduce its registered capital and cancel the shares in accordance with the law.

After this ruling of the Wuxi Intermediate People's Court took legal effect, the debt owed by the enforcee Hengtong Company to the applicant for enforcement Xinjiangnan Company was satisfied. Meanwhile, Hengtong Company's shareholding in Xinjiangnan Company correspondingly decreased from 44 million shares to 4,576,162 shares. The legal procedures for Xinjiangnan Company to cancel the shares have been completed, and a new shareholders' meeting has been convened, electing and forming a new board of directors and management team. Currently, Xinjiangnan Company is operating in good condition.
